children: US stocks tumbled on Thursday, with technology shares leading the sell-off as investors pared their exposure to the sector following the post-election rally. The Nasdaq Composite plunged 3.9%, wiping out the previous session's gains and slipping into correction territory, more than 10% below its record high set last month. The S&P 500 fell 2.8%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1,153 points, or 2.2%. Gains in Chevron and Johnson & Johnson failed to offset losses across technology stocks, leaving the Dow with most of its gains from Wednesday's post-election surge erased.
Among the key companies scheduled to announce their second-quarter results on Friday are Hindalco Industries and Tata Steel.

Brent crude rose as traders took stock of Wednesday’s sharp selloff, when the Democratic sweep in US midterm elections sent oil down almost 9%. The global benchmark traded near $97 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate edged above $89 after falling the most since May in the previous session.

Bitcoin tumbled to a seven-week low as a rout in technology shares spilled into risky assets, hurting sentiment in digital assets already under pressure from industry-specific woes. The original cryptocurrency was trading below $76,000 after dropping as much as 5.8%. The selloff came as the Nasdaq 100 plunged 6.4%, led by chipmakers amid underwhelming earnings outlooks and concerns that Democratic control of Congress could bring tighter oversight of the artificial-intelligence industry.

Following their Q2 results, stocks of Britannia, Titan and Bharti Airtel will be in focus after reporting strong performances, while Glenmark Pharma and ONGC may see a reaction to their year-on-year decline in net profit.

title: Market Pulse: Key triggers to watch before the November 6 trading session
